key_insight: Combining structured EHR features, clinical-text embeddings, and knowledge-grounded entity extraction improved sensitivity for 30-day diabetic readmission prediction, but slightly reduced AUROC.
clinical_relevance: The framework could help identify more patients who are later readmitted, though its low specificity raises concerns about false-positive alerts.
method: Fuse engineered EHR features with 32 compressed Bio_ClinicalBERT embedding components.
Extract symbolic entities using a clinical language model, hybrid retrieval, re-ranking, and negation auditing.
Predict readmission with cost-sensitive XGBoost and a threshold calibrated using Youden’s J.
evidence_signal: With a patient-grouped 80/20 split and 20,153 held-out encounters, sensitivity rose from 0.5839 to 0.6667 and Brier score improved from 0.1080 to 0.0977, while AUROC fell from 0.6477 to 0.6375.
watch_item: External and prospective validation are needed; performance on a separate 500-note Hinglish benchmark does not establish real-world multilingual clinical utility.
paper_title: A Neurosymbolic Multimodal Framework for 30-Day Diabetic Readmission Prediction: Integrating Structured EHR Data, Dense Clinical Embeddings, and Knowledge-Grounded Symbolic Extraction
